notes_on_rating: Collecting data just before leaving fits every theft hypothesis, and a scientist taking a copy of her own work before leaving also fits H4. H3 treats the resignation as a coincidence, so it neither predicts nor rules out this item, which on its own discriminates little.

H4 rated C on purpose: by itself, an unapproved remote tool calling overseas could be shadow IT (for example, a researcher working with overseas collaborators). Item 6 rules that out. H2 and H5 say nothing about the tool, so NA.

H4 rated I: the credentials were used from a never-before-seen device two days after the email was opened, which goes against 'the phishing email was not acted on maliciously' (assumption A4: the device has not been verified as a new personal device). Spear-phishing senior scientists with a journal-portal lure fits both H1 and H3.

H3 rated I: criminals send stolen data to infrastructure they control, not to an employee's named personal cloud account on her own workstation. H4 rated C because the scenario itself gives a 'policy-violating personal backup habit' as a possible innocent explanation, which item 9 then undermines.

evidence_item: 5. No extortion contact or leak-site activity
notes_on_rating: Only H3 predicts extortion or resale. The I is soft: this is absence of evidence over a short window, and some criminals hold data or sell it quietly. Espionage actors and insiders do not normally extort.

evidence_item: 6. C2 infrastructure overlap with known APT
notes_on_rating: This is the most diagnostic item for the technical side. It is the only item that says who runs the RAT, and it contradicts both a criminal operator (H3) and an innocent tool (H4). The caveat is that it rests on one SSL-certificate match, attributed with moderate confidence by a second vendor, and certificates are often shared between actors and sometimes planted as false flags. H2 and H5 do not address the RAT, so NA.

This item feels incriminating and discriminates almost nothing. Moving to a rival is ordinary under H4 and a career step under H2; under H1 the rival is a recruitment route, and under H5 it is the beneficiary. 'Same general region' is too vague to tie the firm to item 2.

The ACL fault explains how she reached the files and says nothing about why, so it fits every hypothesis that involves her. It started about six weeks ago, before the phishing (about three weeks ago), so the intruder did not create it.

This is the most diagnostic item for the insider side. H4 rated I: a personal backup of her own work would not include another project's manufacturing-cost and supply-chain files. H2 rated C only because H2 covers data 'useful at her new employer'; commercial cost data from someone else's project fits directed collection (H1, H5) more naturally than career self-interest. H3 does not involve her download, so NA.

A small footprint (one phished account plus the insider) fits a low-and-slow APT and also a lone insider. H3 rated I (soft): double-extortion crews usually move laterally and escalate privileges before stealing data. H4 rated C because 'nothing widespread' is what a false alarm looks like. The phished account's anomaly was already counted under item 3.

The ISAC advisory fits H1, H3 and H4 (Aurora caught up in a broad wave), so it confirms little. It also lowers the weight of item 3: Aurora was probably not singled out, which makes the timing of the phishing next to the resignation more plausibly coincidental.

evidence_item: E12 [ADDED, derived inference from items 2+4]: Exfiltration channel divergence: insider data left through a DLP-visible personal cloud account, not through the RAT/C2 channel already in the division
notes_on_rating: This row is my own inference from items 2 and 4, not a scenario fact. H1 rated I only against its coordinated-insider version: a state service with a working implant in the division would not usually have its asset upload through a traceable personal account. The I is soft, because services sometimes keep insiders and implants separate on purpose. H3 rated NA to avoid counting item 4 twice.
The tally informs the judgment without deciding it. H2 and H5 reach 0 partly because they are NA on the four technical items they do not explain. H4's three Is carry more weight than H3's four.
